name: files
title: Files
description: Search files by name through the system's index: Spotlight on macOS, fd, locate or find on Linux; by contents too, as a second section or alone with a ' prefix; the recently used files before you type, and as a palette of their own. Enter on a folder browses it (sorted by name, date or size, `..` and `←` up). Open, open with another app, reveal, Quick Look, open in a terminal, copy the path, the file or the text in an image (OCR), rename, move or copy to a folder, compress, trash.
author: pal

settings.label: Results
settings.description: At most this many rows per query.

settings.label: Hidden files
settings.text: List files and folders whose name starts with a dot

settings.label: Search contents
settings.text: Also list files whose text contains the query, under the name matches (a query starting with ' or content: searches contents only)

settings.label: OCR copies are private
settings.text: Text read from an image (Copy text) is kept out of clipboard history

settings.label: Exclude
settings.description: Folders skipped below the search folders, by name (`node_modules`) or a short path (`Library/Caches`).

settings.label: Terminal
settings.description: What Open in Terminal opens: `Terminal` (default), `iTerm`, `kitty`, `Alacritty`, `WezTerm`, `Ghostty`, or any app name (`open -na <name> --args -e ...`); on Linux a command name (`kitty`, `foot`, `alacritty`, `wezterm`, `ghostty`, ...), else `$TERMINAL`, else the first of those installed.

store.tagline: File search over the OS index, recent files before you type
features: Spotlight (`mdfind -name`) on macOS; `fd`, else `locate`, else a bounded `find` on Linux, one process per keystroke, killed after 3 s
Exact and prefix name matches first, at most `limit` rows, the folder as the subtitle, size and date on the right

Contents too: files whose text has the query as a second section, the first matching line as the subtitle (Spotlight's text index on macOS, `rg` or `grep` on Linux, 1 s at most); `'query` or `content:query` searches contents only
Copy text (OCR, `cmd+shift+t`) on an image or a PDF's first page: the Vision framework on macOS, `tesseract` on Linux
Before you type: the files used in the last seven days; the same rows as the Recent Files palette

Enter (or `→`) on a folder browses it as a level whose crumb is the folder: a `..` row (`←` or Backspace goes up from anywhere), the entries sorted by name, date or size from the dropdown, pictures with their thumbnails, `cmd+.` for hidden files; `~/` or `/` typed lists that folder the same way
Open with… (`cmd+o`) lists the apps the OS registers for the file, the default tagged
Reveal (`cmd+enter`), Quick Look (`cmd+y`), Copy path (`cmd+c`), Copy file (`cmd+shift+c`), Open in Terminal (`cmd+t`, the folder or the file's), Move to Trash (`cmd+d`, asks first)
Rename (`cmd+shift+r`), Move to (`cmd+m`) and Copy to (`cmd+alt+c`) a folder, each a form; Compress (`cmd+shift+z`) zips the file, or every marked row, next to it
The detail pane: path, size, modified, kind, an image's pixel size and Finder's tags (Spotlight, macOS), and the first 40 lines of a text file

screenshots.caption: Part of a file name typed: the matches under the configured folders, size and date on the right
The detail pane on a text file: path, size, modified, kind, and its first lines
Open with…: the apps registered for the file, the default tagged
Recent Files: what was used in the last seven days, newest first
Browsing ~/proj: the crumb is the folder, .. leads, the dropdown sorts by name, date or size
Rename, Move to and Copy to are forms; Compress zips the file next to itself

actions.title: Show hidden files
actions.description: In a browsed folder: flips the `show_hidden` setting.

files.description: Type part of a file name; rows are the matches under the configured folders. Before you type: the recently used files. A path (`~/Down`, `/usr/local`) lists the file or its completions, at the root too, and a path ending in `/` lists that folder whole; Enter on a folder browses it. A root query nothing matched gets a Search Files fallback row.

keys.title: Open the file, browse a folder

browse.description: A folder's contents, pushed by Browse on a folder row (or by typing a path ending in `/`): a `..` row first, then the entries under the dropdown's sort (name, date, size), hidden ones with `show_hidden`, at most 500. The crumb is the folder; typing filters by name.

keys.title: Browse a folder, open a file
Browse the folder under the cursor
Cycle the sort: name, date, size

recent.description: Files used in the last seven days under the configured folders, newest first.
